thesis: The 60-day decline follows a confirmed, company-disclosed structural event: an underwritten public offering of 210,526,315 shares at $95, upsized to $20B from $15B and closed August 12, 2026, adding roughly 4.2% to the pre-offering share count and up to 4.8% if underwriters exercise their option on a further 31.6 million shares. The stock closed at $87.26 today, still below that $95 issue price. Two disclosed operating problems compound it rather than one dominating: the foundry unit lost $2.1B in Q2 even as its revenue grew 31%, and Intel's CPU market share has fallen to a three-decade low. The strongest counter-case is that foundry revenue is growing 31% and the raise funds capex from a position of chosen strength, but that does not resolve a loss of that size against a permanently larger share count. A US Supreme Court oral argument in the Intel 401(k) case is set for October, an unresolved event inside the next 90 days. This suggests a disclosed, permanent change in share count layered on deteriorating share position, which argues against a new entry here.
invalidation: Foundry losses narrow materially in Q3 results, or the stock reclaims and holds the $95 offering price on disclosed operating progress rather than on sector beta.

thesis: Marvell's 60-day decline is primarily sector-driven — a broad sell-off in AI and semiconductor names on skepticism about AI capex payback — rather than a company-specific disclosure, and the stock fell a further 4.08% today to $229.32. Company-level evidence is genuinely offsetting: JPMorgan reiterated Overweight today, calling Marvell a top chip pick and saying the data-center story has strengthened over the past 90 days on optical, switching and custom silicon, and an expanded Google partnership is reported at $12.2B with up to $120B of revenue through 2033; against that sit earlier reports that Amazon may have moved next-generation Trainium design work to a competitor. Second-quarter results land August 27 after the close, three days out — an unresolved binary event that could reverse the read in either direction. No lawsuit or investigation with a scheduled ruling, hearing, or deadline in the next 90 days surfaced, and no restatement, auditor dismissal, or executive indictment within the last three years surfaced. This suggests waiting for the print rather than entering ahead of it.
invalidation: August 27 results confirm custom-silicon design-win losses, or guidance falls materially short of the growth the Google expansion implies.

thesis: Alliance Laundry's qualifying signal is driven by a disclosed share-supply event, not by operating results. An upsized public offering of common stock by selling stockholder BDT Capital Partners priced August 18, and the stock has fallen eight consecutive sessions for a cumulative 14%, erasing about $761M of market value; today's 3.00x volume spike is the mechanical footprint of that distribution rather than new fundamental news. The strongest counter-case is that the underlying business is performing: Q2 2026 results released August 13 showed revenue of $476.8M up 7%, net income of $68.7M, adjusted EPS of $0.41 and adjusted EBITDA up about 12%, with North America revenue up 9%. That does not resolve the setup, because the offering is a secondary by the principal holder rather than new issuance, so the pressure is ongoing distribution of existing stock into a thin float, and the price sits only about 0.3% above its 200-day moving average — a further move down would put it below trend. No lawsuit with a scheduled ruling in the next 90 days and no restatement, auditor dismissal, or executive indictment in the last three years surfaced. This suggests an unfinished distribution rather than a clean entry.
invalidation: The offering is fully absorbed and the stock reclaims its pre-offering range on volume returning to normal, without breaking its 200-day moving average.

thesis: Fiscal Q3 2026 (June quarter) delivered confirmed, company-disclosed record results: quarterly sales records for iPhone, Mac and Services simultaneously, with revenue up in every geographic segment, and Apple has authorized the largest buyback in its history. The strongest counter-evidence is the leadership change — Tim Cook hands the CEO role to John Ternus on September 1, and Apple has dropped the net-cash-neutral target it set in 2018, which points to heavier AI and R&D spending and therefore a smaller share of cash returned. That does not change the read: the succession was announced months in advance and is an orderly, planned handoff rather than a departure tied to execution problems, and the record June-quarter results and the already-authorized repurchase are settled facts independent of how the next CEO allocates incremental capital. On litigation, the DOJ antitrust case has no trial date, is in settlement talks and is not expected to reach trial before 2027, and the $490M securities-fraud class action received final court approval back in September 2024 — no scheduled ruling falls in the next 90 days. This suggests the pullback from the late-July record repriced expectations rather than the disclosed business.
invalidation: Fiscal Q4 (September quarter) results in late October show Services growth decelerating from its record run-rate, or the buyback authorization goes unexecuted under the new CEO.
sources: Apple Inc. SEC Form 10-Q FY2026 Q3: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019326000020/aapl-20260627.htm
Bloomberg Law (securities settlement final approval, Sept 2024): https://news.bloomberglaw.com/securities-law/apples-490-million-securities-fraud-settlement-gets-court-nod

thesis: Q2 2026 results reported August 4 are a confirmed, company-disclosed acceleration: revenue of $11.5B with data-center revenue up 107% year over year to $6.7B, and management guiding data-center sales to double again in 2027 with second-half server revenue up more than 80%. Helios, AMD's first rack-scale AI system, begins shipping this quarter to Meta, OpenAI and Oracle. The strongest counter-evidence is that the stock fell anyway and is down about 12.6% over the past month, because expectations were extreme after a roughly 140% year-to-date run and the market turned skeptical on AI capex broadly. That does not overturn the disclosed trajectory — data-center revenue more than doubled year over year and the guidance is for another doubling — but it does cap the read, because the strongest forward element is guidance rather than a completed event, and the near-term price driver remains sector positioning with NVIDIA reporting August 26. No lawsuit with a scheduled ruling in the next 90 days and no restatement, auditor dismissal, or executive indictment in the last three years surfaced. This suggests multiple compression against accelerating disclosed fundamentals.
invalidation: Q3 2026 results or guidance show data-center growth decelerating from the disclosed trajectory, or the stock loses its 200-day moving average near $331.

thesis: SpaceX's decline since its June 12, 2026 Nasdaq listing at $135 is dominated by a disclosed and still-unfinished share-supply schedule rather than an operating change. A staggered lockup will free about 88% of roughly 13 billion shares through 2027; more than 900 million shares unlocked on August 6 and a further 319 million became tradable last week, with a 1.3 billion-share tranche due around third-quarter earnings in early November and the 180-day expiry in December — reporting puts the total potential release at about $116B of stock. Elon Musk's own 6.42 billion shares stay locked until June 2027. A company-specific operational setback also contributed: the July 16 Starship launch was aborted after several engines failed, and the planned August catch attempt has slipped. The counter-case is that the stock has repeatedly reclaimed its $135 IPO price and rose 6% on one unlock day, so supply is being absorbed. That leaves the read unresolved rather than settled, with the two largest tranches still ahead. Texas property-owner suits filed April 30, 2026 remain pending with no scheduled ruling in the next 90 days. This suggests a persistent overhang rather than a clean entry.
invalidation: The November and December tranches clear without the stock breaking back below the $135 IPO price, alongside a completed Starship flight.
